attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.5.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, Ubuntu 16.04, Erlang 18.3) with AMQP exposed only over TLS (5671) using a purpose-built CA. The CA (generated on node1) issued per-node server certs (CN/IP SANs matching each node) and one client cert used for mutual TLS. rabbitmq.config on every node sets tcp_listeners=[] (no plaintext AMQP), ssl_listeners=[5671], and ssl_options with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, so only clients presenting a certificate signed by the cluster CA can connect — verified by both positive (CA-issued client cert succeeds, TLS handshake + AMQP publish/consume works) and negative (no cert and a cert from an unrelated self-signed CA both fail with an SSL "handshake failure"/"bad certificate" alert) tests. The management UI (15672) is bound to each node's private cluster IP only (not 0.0.0.0/loopback) and additionally firewalled via iptables to accept only the 10.100.106.0/24 cluster subnet, with the rule persisted via iptables-persistent. Cluster formed via join_cluster with a shared Erlang cookie; verified no partitions and matching membership from all three nodes' perspectives. End-to-end functional proof: a message published on node1 over mutual-TLS AMQP was consumed on node3, confirming real cluster state sharing (not just membership metadata).\n\nMandatory restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id + cluster/TLS/mgmt health on all nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned first). For each node: confirmed SSH/exec was briefly unavailable, polled until it returned, proved a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, confirmed rabbitmq-server auto-started and rejoined with full 3-node quorum and zero partitions, and re-applied+persisted the 15672 firewall rule (iptables rules were not persistent by default and needed re-saving after each reboot — now installed via iptables-persistent so they survive future reboots). After all three restarts, re-ran the mutual-TLS publish (node1) / consume (node2) test successfully, confirming the cluster and its TLS/auth posture are fully intact post-restart.
